A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BridgePure and the same protection-leakage threat model. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison. Renumbered and relocated experiments can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracies, image-quality measurements, style-mimicry outputs, and ablation and transfer experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds purification comparisons, style-transfer experiments, dilution results, and an early-stopping result in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Both versions use paired-data DDBM training, the same score-matching objective, endpoint-conditioned hybrid sampling, and optional Gaussian preprocessing. No new BridgePure component or procedural change is stated. Corrections to the background SDE formulas do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Monet paintings as training data for purification of @nulevoy artwork and tests Glaze-to-Mist and Mist-to-Glaze transfer for style mimicry (Appendices C.9–C.10). This extends artist and mismatch-scenario coverage within an existing task; the classification datasets and principal target artwork remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 introduces direct painting-purification comparisons against GrIDPure, PDM, and NoisyUpscaling in Appendix C.4 and Figures 11–12. v1's artwork experiments contain no corresponding competing-purifier comparison; mentioning Noisy Upscaling in related work did not constitute evaluation. The classification comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 changes reported BridgePure batch sizes from 32 to 256 for CIFAR-10/100 and from 4 to 16 for artwork, while retaining 100,000 training steps. These substantially revise the stated training budgets, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. v2 also adds a 40,000-step early-stopping evaluation and a 500-image dilution control.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of cross-protection and cross-artist transfer for style mimicry, a detailed brushstroke-preservation comparison with PDM, early-stopping evidence, and an equal-data-budget dilution comparison. These extend scrutiny of applicability, fidelity, efficiency, and the value of paired leakage. The mixed-protection experiment and earlier classification ablations are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: The five-trial mean-and-standard-deviation practice in Table 1 is unchanged. Locally, v2 Table 6 drops the clean-baseline standard deviations shown in v1 Table 4, displaying 94.01 and 74.27 alone. Those deviations remain available in Table 1, so this is a limited reporting omission, not evidence of changed statistical procedures.

E6.justification: The retained classification tables preserve their accuracy values. Substantial additions concern painting-purification quality and transfer, new dilution results, and early stopping. For example, v2 Table 5 reports 500-image dilution averages of 49.3% and 24.0%, versus BridgePure's 91.9% and 70.3% on CIFAR-10/100. Appendix C.1 newly reports 87.88/87.87/87.61% for EM/LSP/TAP after 40,000 training steps; these are additional-condition results, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 corrects Equation (2) so dt multiplies the complete bridge drift. Equation (3) changes the reverse-SDE score coefficient from one-half to one and restores the g(t) noise multiplier. These are substantive mathematical corrections, while the theoretical framework remains unchanged and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that limited paired protection leakage enables BridgePure to circumvent black-box protections and outperform baselines on classification and style mimicry without large-scale diffusion pretraining. The revised title and expanded introduction emphasize this existing contribution. Image fidelity and mitigation receive greater prominence, but the three principal contributions and conclusion retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies transferability by task, explaining successful artwork transfer alongside the retained classification limitations, and adds an argument about amortized computational cost. Appendix D.1 substantially expands mitigation discussion into restricted API access, avoiding offline services, deployment-specific configurations, and ownership/style verification. These are proposed countermeasures, not experimentally validated defenses.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies 224×224 processing, batch size 16, and A100 hardware for Cars/Pets, while revising the reported CIFAR and artwork batch sizes. Appendix C.1 supplies the early-stopping budget and 450-minute training time. The Cars/Pets additions document existing experiments rather than establish changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v2 adds GrIDPure and PDM to the purification literature, replaces the Huang et al. watermark citation attached to IMPRESS with the IMPRESS paper by Cao et al., and adds the CIFAR technical-report reference. These are limited literature updates; the principal positioning around protection leakage and diffusion bridges remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, edits and expands parts of the abstract and introduction, renames Section 2, and reorganizes Appendix C, including moving mixed-protection discussion from the main text. It also adds Appendix D. The six-section main narrative and much of the existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 extensively compresses and rearranges the main-text displays: Figure 1 uses wrapped text, Figures 3–4 sit side by side, and Figures 5 and 7 use horizontal arrangements. Figure 2 becomes a condensed comparison, with the detailed comparison in Figure 14. New painting-comparison and transfer figures and the dilution table substantially expand the displays. Figure 7 retains an outdated top/bottom caption after its horizontal rearrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the previously limited comparative evidence for artwork purification, tests additional transfer conditions, adds an equal-budget dilution control, and repairs incorrect SDE formulas. These improve support and correctness while retaining the core method and principal classification results. The gains remain bounded: new artwork evidence is qualitative, the reason for revised batch sizes is unexplained, and compressed figures introduce some readability and caption problems.
